data.description:
Previously recovered archive records show ntfy used as a temporary program/message surface by several automated, agent-like workflows. This standalone redacted ZIP inventories all classified retained 2026 links recovered in the named local evidence set, with topic, original URL as inert text, archive reference, capture time, confidence, task attribution, body availability and source/hash provenance. It does not classify all 491 background topics or all 521 message/API captures as agent activity.

The strongest task families are: Erroll Garner recording acquisition and numerical pitch analysis matching two HLE note/scale questions; five Mayo symptom-checker programs matching DeepSearchQA 505 through the same two forms and factors; and Sky Island Journal/Andrea Damic article identification combined with the 40-topic Tomás Kopecký search burst, matching BrowseComp 339. The ZIP includes all 37 July 8 input/output pairs and every input program, available output messages, all 40 Kopecký topics with missing-body status, and the earlier Garner/Mayo evidence. The programs and message bodies are inert text. Long state/token/encoded literals are redacted, including carriers that could otherwise preserve secrets. Third-party article/audio content is withheld; source URLs, hashes and concise task metadata remain.

These records establish task-specific automation and associated archived status/results, not a named provider, a single operator, or membership in the collusion.wiki population. Exact benchmark matches identify a task; they do not identify who ran it. Short go/START/OK/IMG markers are low-confidence candidates. June/July execution probes have no exact content benchmark. September claim/run/scout/reciprocal-fire coordination is retained as separate later activity, not merged into the earlier actor hypothesis.

CDC topic wqz58 contains a program submitting a form to the D158 endpoint. A preserved CDC HTTP 500 query-validation response is captured one second later. Code, target and timing support a submission workflow but not a complete initiating-session trace. No mortality results, suppression bypass or reidentification are shown. DeepSearchQA 506 is only a weak candidate: the script has the endpoint but lacks the substantive query dimensions. This corrects stronger wording in the historical report.

Archive handling matters. Arbitrary ntfy topic pages can return a generic HTML shell without messages. GET /publish/send/trigger URLs can create messages when crawled; a captured triggered message or publication endpoint alone is not agent proof. Such original URLs and program-carrier archive references are retained only as inert strings with local evidence, never clickable action links. Input/output association and recorded results are stronger than a simple callback marker, but publication responses do not identify the initiator. Original capture times and message times are not interchangeable.

Excluded: malformed/mytopic documentation GET /publish crawler artifacts, monitoring/IP-grabber and private-user notification bodies, 2025 captures, unrelated tunnel advertisements, generic triggered-only topics, and the RajaDairy ZIP filename-only lead. The main inventory covers 143 core topics. A separate supplement contains 19 ambiguous probe-marker topics with task and AI identity unknown. No topic names were guessed; only already-recovered local references were used. Failed older fetch metadata is distinguished from actual later local body files.
data.summary: Agent activity on ntfy.sh, benchmark matches to Humanity's Last Exam and DeepSearchQA
